content.title: Scale Spectacle Ladder | Reset the Reference, Move Closer
content.summary: Each short segment resets a familiar viewpoint and scale reference before introducing one impossible aerial form. Reduce the distance through clear changes in occlusion and apparent size, then end with a close encounter.

quick_start.input_format: 5 familiar scale references + 1 giant original form per mirror + viewpoint changes + gradually shortening distance + close final state
quick_start.recommended_input: Five original giant aerial seed structures appear successively in the wind field, train window, quarry, greenhouse and maintenance vehicle viewpoint, each time the distance is closer, and finally passing directly above the roof of the vehicle.
required_anchors: Give each vignette an immediately familiar scale anchor.
Use one dominant impossible silhouette per vignette.
Increase proximity, not just nominal size.
End with a viewpoint-level encounter that preserves spatial legibility.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Each short segment resets a familiar viewpoint and scale reference before introducing one impossible aerial form. Reduce the distance through clear changes in occlusion and apparent size, then end with a close encounter.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Reset a familiar viewpoint and scale anchor in each vignette, introduce one impossible airborne form that preserves readable silhouette, vary observer distance and occlusion, then escalate proximity until the final viewpoint encounter feels immediate rather than merely larger.

invariants.rule: Give each vignette an immediately familiar scale anchor.
invariants.ablation_failure: A blank sky provides no scale proof.

invariants.rule: Use one dominant impossible silhouette per vignette.
invariants.ablation_failure: Several equal forms create visual noise.

invariants.rule: Change observer carrier or occlusion between vignettes.
Increase proximity, not just nominal size.
invariants.purpose: Creates a real escalation toward encounter.

invariants.rule: End with a viewpoint-level encounter that preserves spatial legibility.
invariants.ablation_failure: An abstract final close-up loses the observer relationship.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair whose role is clear without source identity.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A materially new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific location.

slots.name: causal_carrier
slots.constraint: One object, route, mark or device that visibly carries the causal chain.

slots.name: state_change
slots.constraint: Five ordered states with observable handoffs, not a decorative montage.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: A new proof-oriented information order that does not copy source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A held final consequence that resolves or recontextualizes the setup.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of story-world cues supporting each visible change.

anti_copy_exclusions: source giant whale, manta, nautilus, jellyfish and shark
Shanghai skyline, airplane window, highway and car POV
the exact animal order and city landmarks
